Package org.aeonbits.owner.handlers

Interface ValueHandler

All Superinterfaces:
Serializable
All Known Implementing Classes:
AesGcmHandler, JndiHandler, RsaHandler
public interface ValueHandler extends Serializable
Turns the payload of a ${$name::payload} marker into the value that replaces it.

The marker

A value can name a handler instead of holding its own text: 

     db.password = ${$aes-gcm::c2FsdAAAAAAAAAAAaXYAAAAAAAAAY2lwaGVy}
     api.token   = ${$vault::secret/data/app:v2}
     tls.key     = ${$file::/run/secrets/tls.key}

The library reads the envelope - the leading $, the name, the :: - and hands everything after the first :: to the handler registered under that name, as text. The library owns the envelope and the handler owns the payload: nothing between the :: and the closing brace is interpreted here, so a handler that wants parameters, versions or paths defines them in whatever syntax suits it.

The only rule a payload must respect is that it cannot contain a }, which is what ends the expression. Base64 never produces one; a path or a URL never does either.

Being expansion is the point

A marker is resolved by the same substitution that resolves ${other.key}, which is what makes it reach everywhere a value can be read rather than only the methods of a Config interface:

  • fill gets the resolved value, because fill expands;
  • a value that refers to one - jdbc.url=...${db.password} - gets the resolved value too, because expansion recurses into what it finds;
  • store writes the marker back, because the properties hold its text and not its answer.

What a handler must not do

Answer with the empty string when it cannot answer. A marker names a value that has to come from somewhere, so failing to produce it is a configuration error and must be thrown, not returned. This is the same reasoning that makes an unregistered name an error rather than a fallback: for a password, the empty string is the worst available answer, and it is indistinguishable from success.

Expect its answer to be expanded. It is not. What a handler returns replaces the marker verbatim, ${ included - a decrypted secret that happens to contain one is a secret, not a template.

Getting a handler into a factory

One way, deliberately: 

     ConfigFactory.registerValueHandler(new AesGcmHandler(passphrase));

Unlike a Loader, a handler is not discovered on the classpath. A file format found on the classpath and enabled by itself reads files that are already yours; a handler found on the classpath and enabled by itself would answer for values in them. Registration also settles where a handler's own configuration comes from - a passphrase, a token, an endpoint - since the caller constructs the instance and brings it.

Why this is Serializable, and the one trap in it

A configuration object can be serialized, and it holds the handlers registered on the factory that created it - the same arrangement as Loader. So a handler travels in the serialized form of every configuration that factory made, whether or not any of them uses a marker.

Which is why a handler should not be an anonymous or an inner class. Both capture the instance that created them, so registering one drags that object into the graph, and a configuration that has nothing to do with it fails to serialize with a NotSerializableException naming a class nobody would think to look at. A static class, or a top-level one, has nothing to capture.

Key material is the other half of this: AesGcmHandler and RsaHandler keep their passphrase and their private key transient, so that serializing a configuration never writes a secret into a file nobody chose to protect. Anything a handler holds that is a secret should do the same, and say so when it is asked to work without it.

  • Method Details

    • name

      String name()
      The name this handler answers to, which is what appears between ${$ and ::.

      It is the identifier of what the handler does, and the reason there is no registry of numbers here: a second construction arrives as a second name. It is also where a key rotation goes - aes-gcm-2024 registered beside aes-gcm-2025 turns a rotation into an edit to the file, one value at a time.

      A name may not be empty, and may not contain whitespace or any of $ : { }: those are what tell a marker apart from an ordinary key, and a name using them would not be reachable.

      Returns:
      the name, never null.

    • resolve

      String resolve(String payload)
      Resolves the payload of a marker into the value that replaces it.
      Parameters:
      payload - everything after the first :: and before the closing brace, as written, except that any ${...} inside it has already been expanded.
      Returns:
      the value, which replaces the whole marker and is not expanded further.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the payload cannot be resolved. Throwing is the contract: returning null or the empty string reports a failure as a value.
